newsitem.title: USA: Envirodyne opposes Zapata board proposal.
newsitem.headline: Envirodyne opposes Zapata board proposal.

text.p: Envirodyne Industries Inc said Tuesday it will "vigorously oppose" efforts by investor Malcolm Glazer to replace all of its directors.

The company said Glazer, through Zapata Corp, wants to take control without paying a fair price to Envirodyne's shareholders. Envirodyne pledged to prevent Zapata from gaining control at the expense of other shareholders.
Zapata is Envirodyne's largest stockholder, with a 40.1 percent stake in the food packaging and food service supplier.

In a letter to Glazer, Envirodyne said the slate of directors proposed by Glazer, including three of his sons and the person who handles his public relations activities, do not have the necessary experience or independence to effectively serve on its board.
Zapata officials were not available for comment.
Envirodyne said it remains willing to carefully consider any bona fide proposal to acquire the company at a fair price.
Envirodyne shares closed down 1/8 Tuesday at 6-1/2.

Envirodyne said Zapata made the propsoal in a filing last month with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. Glazer and his son Avram currently serve on Envirodyne's board, although they were not slated for reelection after Malcolm Glazer refused to agree not to seek control of the company for the next 12 months, Envirodyne said.
Envirodyne has nominated its own slate of directors for reelection at its board meeting.
